title: Eshrefids
capsule: The Eshrefids (Eşrefoğulları) were a Turkmen Anatolian beylik centred on Beyşehir in the lake district of south-central Anatolia, one of several frontier principalities that emerged from the collapse of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in the late thirteenth century. The dynasty's founder Suleiman ibn Eshref Bey established control over the Beyşehir region around 1280–1290 and his successor Mubariz al-Din Mehmed Bey briefly extended authority over Eğirdir and parts of the former Hamidid lands. The beylik was absorbed by the expanding Germiyanid-allied Karamanid confederation in 1326, when the last Eshrefid ruler was executed by Timurtash, the Mongol Ilkhanid governor of Anatolia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik is attested in Ilkhanid and early Ottoman sources, but territorial extent is poorly defined and relies on inferences from later cadastral and narrative sources.
